$schemaNote: Golden vectors for the binary terminal data-plane frame codec (S2). SSOT - do NOT copy this file. The frontend codec test (S4) must read THIS path. See 06-work-plan.md S2-a and 05:452.
$handComputed: Every hexFrame here was computed by hand from the byte-offset tables in docs/research/binary-comms/01-frame-format-and-negotiation.md (header 01:45-52, OUTPUT prologue 01:522-528, segment 01:532-538, SCREEN_SNAPSHOT prologue 01:550, CHECKPOINT_CHUNK prologue 01:556). The two checkpoint-start-* vectors derive instead from the 07-prologue-spec-remaining-opcodes.md annex that 01 section 1.8 incorporates by reference - layout 07 section 2.9, lease slot 07 section 2.6.1, flags2 bit table 07:420-429 - because 01 section 1.8 carries only the 200-byte total (revision R1) and delegates the offsets. Their flags2 must agree with which offsets carry a value: bit0 clear means off 128 is zero, which is the rule the first draft of these two vectors broke.. No hexFrame was produced by dumping encoder output - that would make the round-trip assertion vacuous (05:450, memory check_operands_must_have_independent_origins). Two devices keep the hand computation auditable: (1) every vector carries a `layout` array whose rows are [byteOffset, hexBytes, meaning]; the test asserts the rows are contiguous from 0 and that their concatenation equals hexFrame, so a typo in either form is red. (2) fault cases are expressed as `derivedFrom` patches of a layout-verified vector, so the only hand-written part of a fault is the 1-2 bytes that create the fault.

vectors.name: output-minimal-52
vectors.note: Minimum valid OUTPUT frame: header 28 + prologue 24, payloadLength=24, channelId=1. payloadLength=0 is NOT a valid OUTPUT frame because PROLOGUE_PRESENT is mandatory (01:78 / 01:84).

vectors.name: output-utf8-body-60
vectors.note: P6 - UTF-8 multi-byte preservation. body = "a<U+D55C><U+1F600>" = 0x61 | 0xED 0x95 0x9C | 0xF0 0x9F 0x98 0x80 = 8 bytes (1B + 3B + 4B).

vectors.name: output-two-segments-95
vectors.note: P2 - encode(m).byteLength === 28 + prologueBytes + 16*segmentCount + bodyBytes = 28 + 24 + 32 + 11 = 95. All three segment deltas are relative to the prologue values (01:508).

vectors.name: screen-snapshot-54
vectors.note: 0x02 prologue 24B = seq u64 | cols u16 | rows u16 | mode u8 | truncated u8 | flags2 u16 | authorityRevision u32 | authorityEpochIndex u16 | replayTokenIndex u16 (01:518). flags = 0x0009 (MANDATORY only) - the encoder sets PAYLOAD_UTF8_TEXT for OUTPUT only (01 appendix B2:1384). This vector doubles as the F10 boundary control 'flags = 0x0009 must be accepted'.

vectors.name: checkpoint-chunk-44
vectors.note: 0x05 prologue 12B = chunkIndex u32 | chunkCount u32 | viewGeneration u32 (01:524). Body is raw (base64-decoded) bytes, so PAYLOAD_UTF8_TEXT is not set.

vectors.name: output-ordinal-extremes-52
vectors.note: P5 - u64 ordinals at extremes. streamEpoch = 2^53 = 9007199254740992 = 0x0020000000000000. sourceSeq = 2^64-1 = 18446744073709551615 = 0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF. channelId = 0xFFFFFFFF (last valid channel id, 01:1448). chunkIdBase = 2^53+1 = 9007199254740993 = 0x0020000000000001 - a value NOT representable as a JS number, so a String(Number(...)) round-trip would corrupt it.

vectors.name: output-ordinal-signed-boundary-52
vectors.note: IR-BGSTAB-001 AC-2 mandates proof at 0 / 1 / 2^53-1 / 2^53 / 2^63 / 2^64-1. output-minimal-52 carries 0 and 1, output-ordinal-extremes-52 carries 2^53 and 2^64-1; this vector supplies the two that were missing. Derivation: output-ordinal-extremes-52 fixes 2^53 = 0x0020000000000000, so 2^53-1 = 0x0020000000000000 - 1 = 0x001FFFFFFFFFFFFF = 9007199254740991 (the largest exact JS integer - one below it the double grid is still spacing 1). 2^63 sets only the top bit: top nibble 8, fifteen zero nibbles = 0x8000000000000000, and 2^63 = 2^64/2 = 18446744073709551616/2 = 9223372036854775808. 2^63 is the point where a signed 64-bit read wraps to a negative decimal while every value below it reads the same either way.

vectors.name: output-ordinal-fastpath-boundary-52
vectors.note: Straddles the decoder's own fast/slow branch (binaryFrameCodec.ts readOrdinal64: hi === 0 takes a uint32 shortcut, otherwise BigInt). Every other vector sits far from that seam - the fast-path values are all <= 1000 and the slow-path values are all >= 2^53 - so a signed 32-bit read of either half stays invisible. Derivation, all four as u64 big-endian: 2^31-1 = 2147483647 = 0x7FFFFFFF -> 0x000000007FFFFFFF (last value int32 and uint32 agree on); 2^31 = 2147483648 = 0x80000000 -> 0x0000000080000000 (first value where int32 goes negative); 2^32-1 = 4294967295 = 0xFFFFFFFF -> 0x00000000FFFFFFFF (largest hi === 0 value); 2^32 = 4294967296 = 0x100000000 -> 0x0000000100000000 (first hi !== 0 value, i.e. the first that must take the BigInt path).
layout: streamEpoch = 2147483648 = 2^31 (int32 sign flip, still fast path)

vectors.name: batch-two-output-frames-106
vectors.note: P4 - one WS message = 2 complete frames (01:459). END_OF_BATCH is set on the LAST frame only (01:75); setting it on the first would be batch-terminated-early. Frame A = 53 B (payloadLength 25 = 24 + 1 body byte 'A'), frame B = 53 B (body 'B'). Total 106 B.
layout: A.flags = 0x000A = PAYLOAD_UTF8_TEXT|PROLOGUE_PRESENT (NO END_OF_BATCH - not the last frame)

vectors.name: checkpoint-start-rollback-228
vectors.note: 0x04 on the rollback path: Controller.ts:1592-1593 injects responderLeaseId and boundarySourceSeq, so flags2 carries bit2|bit4 = 0x0014 and the lease slot is populated (07 §2.6.1).
layout: off 74: flags2 = bit0 RETAINED_STATE | bit2 BOUNDARY_SOURCE_SEQ | bit4 RESPONDER_LEASE_ID

vectors.name: checkpoint-start-promotion-228
vectors.note: 0x04 on the promotion path: Controller.ts:761-763 enqueues the message bare, so both presence bits are clear and off 160..199 is entirely zero. Absence must decode as a MISSING KEY, never an empty string.
layout: off 128: retainedStateDigest = 32 x 0x00 (flags2 bit0 clear => must be zero)

faults.name: F1-fault-truncated-header-27
faults.note: output-minimal-52 cut to 27 bytes (the last byte of payloadLength removed). Remaining bytes < 28 (01:935).

faults.name: F1-control-minimum-valid-52
faults.note: The 52-byte minimum valid OUTPUT frame MUST be accepted. If this fails we measured 'empty body unsupported' or 'prologue not implemented', not 'truncation'.

faults.name: F2-fault-length-overrun-142
faults.note: payloadLength declares 124 (= prologue 24 + body 100) but the buffer holds only 28 + 24 + 90 = 142 bytes. 0 + 28 + 124 = 152 > 142 (01:941).

faults.name: F2-control-exact-152
faults.note: Exactly 28 + 124 = 152 bytes must be accepted.

faults.name: F2-control-surplus-153
faults.note: 153 bytes (one surplus byte) must fail with a DIFFERENT code than F2: END_OF_BATCH is set but 28+124=152 is not the buffer end (01:942).

faults.name: F3-fault-unknown-opcode-ff
faults.note: opcode 0xFF is permanently reserved (01:171) - must be an explicit unknown-opcode rejection, never a silent drop.

faults.name: F3-control-max-defined-opcode-07
faults.note: 0x07 terminal-checkpoint:output is the highest defined opcode (01:166) and MUST be accepted. 01 section 1.8 defines no prologue layout for 0x07, so payloadLength carries 8 opaque body bytes.
layout: payloadLength = 8 (opaque - no v1 prologue schema for 0x07)

faults.name: F3-control-min-undefined-opcode-08
faults.note: 0x08 is the first reserved (undefined) opcode (01:167) and MUST be rejected. Identical to the 0x07 vector except byte 1. If 0x07 and 0x08 do not split, the decoder is not checking opcodes.

faults.name: F4-control-exact
faults.note: output-utf8-body-60 declares payloadLength = 32 and the buffer is exactly 28 + 32 = 60 bytes.

faults.name: F4-fault-declared-plus-one
faults.note: output-utf8-body-60 with payloadLength 33 (0x21). 28 + 33 = 61 > 60 -> length-overrun (01:941).

faults.name: F4-fault-declared-minus-one
faults.note: output-utf8-body-60 with payloadLength 31 (0x1F). 28 + 31 = 59 != 60 while END_OF_BATCH is set -> batch-terminated-early (01:942). This MUST differ from the +1 code; if both give the same code the decoder is not reading the length field.

faults.name: F5-control-below-limit
faults.note: bodyBytes = 2097151 (limit-1) -> payloadLength = 2097151 + 24 = 2097175 = 0x00200017. The limit is derived from pty.maxSnapshotBytes (config.schema.ts:77 default 2097152) and applies to the bodyBytes domain, NOT payloadLength (06 section 5 S2-b F5 note). The declared length matches the buffer length, so this exercises the policy bound and not F2.

faults.name: F5-control-at-limit
faults.note: bodyBytes = 2097152 (exactly the limit) -> payloadLength = 2097176 = 0x00200018. Must be accepted.

faults.name: F5-fault-above-limit
faults.note: bodyBytes = 2097153 (limit+1) -> payloadLength = 2097177 = 0x00200019. Must be rejected. payload-limit-exceeded is a decoder POLICY code, deliberately distinct from length-overrun so F5 and F2 do not collapse into one measurement.

faults.name: F5-control-oversized-frame-keeps-the-batch
faults.note: M-3 grading control. batch-two-output-frames-106 with frame B (offset 53) inflated past the body bound: B.payloadLength (offset 53+24 = 77) = 24 + 2097153 = 2097177 = 0x00200019 and 2097152 filler bytes appended to B's existing 1-byte body. Buffer = 106 + 2097152 = 2097258 and B.frameEnd = 53 + 28 + 2097177 = 2097258, so the DECLARED length still matches the buffer exactly - that is what separates this from F2 (length-overrun) and keeps framing sound. Because framing is sound the decoder knows frameEnd and can resume, so payload-limit-exceeded is SCOPED (01:958 grading rule applied to a code 01:934-943 does not list): frame A on channelId 1 must still be delivered. If it were fatal, one oversized frame would erase every later frame of the same WS message - the loss pattern 01:951 argues against.

faults.name: F7-fault-binary-frame-on-json-group
faults.note: A perfectly valid binary frame arriving while the group codec is JSON must fail explicitly, never return silently (01:934).

faults.name: F7-control-binary-frame-on-binary-group
faults.note: The same bytes on a binary group must be processed normally. If this fails, the codec branch itself is broken and F7 measured nothing.

faults.name: F8-fault-json-text-into-binary-decoder
faults.note: A JSON control frame delivered to the binary decoder. The first byte is '{' = 0x7B, which is not the negotiated frameVersion, so it converges on bad-frame-version. The point is that it fails EXPLICITLY rather than being mis-parsed or silently dropped.

faults.name: F9-fault-version-02
faults.note: frameVersion 0x02 != negotiated 0x01 (01:936).

faults.name: F9-fault-version-00
faults.note: frameVersion 0x00 is permanently reserved (01:45) but 01:934-943 has NO dedicated rejection code for it - all of 0x00/0x02/0xFF converge on bad-frame-version (06 section 5 S2-b F9 note, decided). The 'zero-filled buffer' hypothesis is recorded as diagnostic METADATA, not as a code.

faults.name: F9-fault-zero-filled-52
faults.note: The canary case that 01:171 / 01:362 exist for: a 52-byte all-zero buffer must not look like a valid frame.

faults.name: F10-fault-reserved-bit2
faults.note: flags = 0x000F = 0x000B | bit2. bit2 is the abandoned CONTINUATION candidate and sits outside v1 activeFlagMask 0x000B (01:89, 01:91).

faults.name: F10-fault-reserved-bit4
faults.note: flags = 0x001B = 0x000B | bit4.

faults.name: F10-control-full-mask-000b
faults.note: flags = 0x000B (the entire v1 activeFlagMask, 01:86) must be accepted.

faults.name: F10-control-mandatory-only-0009
faults.note: flags = 0x0009 (MANDATORY_FLAGS only, 01:84) must be accepted.

faults.name: F10-control-missing-end-of-batch
faults.note: flags = 0x000A on the LAST frame - END_OF_BATCH missing. Must give batch-not-terminated (01:943), a DIFFERENT code from reserved-flag-set.

faults.name: F11-fault-reserved-channel-zero
faults.note: channelId 0 is permanently reserved and must be rejected as reserved-channel, NOT unknown-channel (01:362, 01:939).

faults.name: F11-control-registered-channel
faults.note: channelId 1 is ACTIVE in defaultContext.channels -> accepted.

faults.name: F11-control-unknown-channel-is-scoped
faults.note: Two-frame batch built from batch-two-output-frames-106 by moving frame A onto channelId 99 (absent from the registry). unknown-channel is a SCOPED error: the frame is skipped and parsing CONTINUES (01:958), so frame B on channelId 1 must still be delivered. If unknown-channel were fatal, or shared a code with reserved-channel, frame B would be lost - exactly the silent drop the issue AC forbids.

faults.name: F11-control-retired-channel-is-silent-but-observable
faults.note: Same batch with frame A on channelId 5, which is RETIRED. It is discarded WITHOUT requesting recovery, but a terminal_binary_retired_channel_frame diagnostic is recorded (01:392, 01:395). Frame B must still be delivered.

faults.name: P7-fault-output-payload-length-zero
faults.note: 28-byte header only, payloadLength = 0. PROLOGUE_PRESENT is mandatory for OUTPUT so a declared payload of 0 cannot hold the 24-byte prologue. 01:934-943 has NO code for this; payload-underrun is a decoder POLICY code (see codec docs). Without this control, 'empty body' and 'no prologue' are indistinguishable.

faults.name: P7-control-output-empty-body
faults.note: payloadLength = 24 (prologue only, segmentCount 0, zero body bytes) is accepted and round-trips.

faults.name: P7-fault-segment-array-underrun
faults.note: segmentCount = 2 declares a 32-byte segment array, but payloadLength is only 24 (0x18) so the array cannot fit. Same length domain as the prologue check -> payload-underrun.

faults.name: P8-fault-empty-binary-ws-message
faults.note: L-1 pin. A zero-byte binary WS message is ACCEPTED as a no-op: the appendix B loop (01:1262) is `while off < byteLength`, so with 0 bytes it never runs and there is no frame to reject. This is recorded deliberately, not inherited by accident. It is not the silent drop the issue AC forbids - that prohibition is about discarding decodable PAYLOAD, and zero bytes carry none. No wire code fits either: `batch-not-terminated` (01:943) is a per-frame verdict and there is no frame, and inventing an 11th code was already rejected for the same structural gap in 06 section 5 S2-b F9. See 06 section 5 S2 'S2 execution outcome' for the recommended disposition (observability at the wiring layer, not a new code).

faults.name: P8-control-one-byte-is-truncated-header
faults.note: The acceptance above holds at EXACTLY zero bytes. One byte is already a rejection, so P8 is not measuring 'the decoder tolerates short buffers' - if this control also passed, the loop guard would be wrong rather than the empty case being intentional.

faults.name: D14-fault-prologue-present-cleared-52
faults.note: D14 (06 section 5 S2-g). A frame that CARRIES its 24-byte prologue but declares PROLOGUE_PRESENT = 0. Hand-derived, not patched, so the whole 52 bytes are auditable against the header table (01:45-52) and the OUTPUT prologue table (01:490-496): it is output-minimal-52 with flags recomputed as END_OF_BATCH|PAYLOAD_UTF8_TEXT = 0x0001|0x0002 = 0x0003, i.e. 0x000B with bit3 subtracted. Every other field is unchanged, so payloadLength 24 still holds the prologue exactly, END_OF_BATCH is set on the only (therefore last) frame, and channelId 1 is ACTIVE - the frame passes every other check and is rejected on bit3 alone. The encoder already refuses to emit exactly this shape (assertEncodableHead: 'PROLOGUE_PRESENT is mandatory and cannot be cleared'); before D14 the decoder accepted it, and closing that asymmetry is the whole point.
layout: payloadLength = 24 = prologue 24 + 16*0 segments + 0 body (the prologue IS present)

faults.name: D14-control-prologue-present-set-52
faults.note: The same frame with bit3 SET (flags = 0x000B) must be accepted. It differs from D14-fault-prologue-present-cleared-52 in exactly the two flag bytes at offset 2, so if this control also failed we would be measuring something other than bit3.

faults.name: D14-control-mid-batch-bit0-cleared
faults.note: THE decisive control for D14. batch-two-output-frames-106 unmodified: frame A carries flags = 0x000A, i.e. END_OF_BATCH (bit0) = 0 because A is not the last frame (01:75). MANDATORY_FLAGS = bit0|bit3 = 0x0009 (01:84) is a NEGOTIATION invariant (01:93), not a per-frame one: 0x000A & 0x0009 = 0x0008 != 0x0009, so a decoder predicate '(flags & MANDATORY_FLAGS) === MANDATORY_FLAGS' would reject frame A and with it every mid-batch frame ever sent. Both frames must decode.

faults.name: D14-control-mid-batch-mandatory-flag-only
faults.note: The tightest form of the control above. Frame A's flags at offset 2 are hand-patched 0x000A -> 0x0008, so A now carries PROLOGUE_PRESENT and nothing else: bit0 = 0 (not the last frame) and bit1 = 0 (the negotiable PAYLOAD_UTF8_TEXT dropped). flags & MANDATORY_FLAGS = 0x0008 != 0x0009 while flags & FLAG_PROLOGUE_PRESENT = 0x0008 != 0. The two candidate predicates give opposite verdicts on this exact frame, and the frame is legal, so it must be accepted. Frame B is untouched and still terminates the batch.

faults.name: D14-fault-mid-batch-prologue-present-cleared
faults.note: The check is per FRAME, not per WS message. batch-two-output-frames-106 with frame B's flags at offset 55 hand-patched 0x000B -> 0x0003: B still terminates the batch (bit0 set) but clears bit3 while carrying its prologue. Frame A (offset 0, flags 0x000A, bit0 already 0) must decode first and survive the fatal that follows at offset 53 - 01:949-960 forbids a fatal from erasing frames already parsed.

patch: B.flags = 0x0003 - bit3 cleared, bit0 still set

faults.name: D14-control-no-prologue-schema-bit3-cleared
faults.note: Opcode 0x07 with flags hand-patched 0x0009 -> 0x0001, i.e. bit3 cleared. This MUST be accepted. 01 section 1.8 defines no prologue layout for 0x03/0x04/0x06/0x07, so prologueBytes() is 0 and such a frame genuinely carries no prologue: for it, SETTING PROLOGUE_PRESENT would be the false statement and clearing it is honest. The encoder cannot emit these opcodes at all (assertEncodableHead rejects prologueBytes === 0), so there is no encoder/decoder asymmetry here for D14 to close, and rejecting would pre-judge the spec gap D15 records. The frame stays opaque.
